prompt.context: Katherine Isaacs is a fitness-focused influencer on several major social media platforms. She posts videos about her workouts, and these videos garner hundreds of thousands of views. While she is excited about her current reach and the steady income she receives from the social media sites, she is considering launching her own app. You have been brought in by her team to help think through whether she should launch an app or just stay with the social media sites.
prompt.question: Should Katherine Isaacs launch her own app?

clarifying_info.a: She would like to generate $30M in additional, annual profits without spending more than 20 hours of her time per week on the app.

clarifying_info.q: What would be on the app?
clarifying_info.a: She is open to many ideas and is looking to you for guidance.

clarifying_info.q: How does she make money now?
clarifying_info.a: She gets paid by the social media sites for driving traffic and she gets paid from companies for products for which she directly advertises in her videos and posts.

clarifying_info.q: How much money does she make now?
clarifying_info.a: She makes $5M in Social Media profits now (revenue and profit — she has no costs for the social media sites).

exhibits.title: Revenue and SM Impact
exhibits.shows: A table listing five potential app products/services with their estimated customer counts (in thousands), annual revenue per customer, and the percentage impact each would have on Katherine's existing social media profit.

rows: Live events and in-app ticket portal
Creating and advertising private label products

exhibits.title: Cost and Hour Requirement
exhibits.shows: A table listing the same five potential app products/services with their estimated annual cost and the hours per week required from Katherine personally.

rows: Live events and in-app ticket portal
Creating and advertising private label products

framework: 1. Financial: Revenue (multiple streams including direct advertising, subscriptions, e-commerce), Costs (fixed: development; variable: maintenance/operational), and impact on existing SM revenue (cannibalization or uplift)
2. Operational: Can Katherine's team build and maintain the app? Does she have the bandwidth given her 20-hr/week constraint?
3. Brand impact: How does an app affect her personal brand and relationship with existing social media platforms?
4. Market: Size (followers with app-enabled phones), Competition (existing fitness/workout apps), Trends (are users shifting to dedicated apps from social media for fitness content?)

questions.prompt: What sorts of products and services could Katherine include on the app?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm a variety of content types and monetization models. Strong answers touch on both products vs. services and content similar to SM vs. new exclusive content. Examples: workout regimen/lessons, live-streamed workouts, products for sale (gear, food/drink), in-person event tickets, personal lifestyle content, multi-influencer platform, gamified rewards, premium/exclusive video subscriptions.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2, calculate the profit per hour for each potential product/service and determine which Katherine should include to meet her goals ($30M additional profit, no more than 20 hrs/week).
questions.guidance: Candidate must: (1) Calculate app revenue = customers × annual revenue per customer. (2) Calculate SM revenue impact = % impact × $5M existing SM profit. Note: impacts are additive across chosen options. (3) Calculate profit = app revenue + SM revenue impact − annual cost. (4) Calculate profit per hour = profit / (hours/week × 52, or treat hours/week as the denominator directly since all figures are annual). Rank by profit per hour. Best combo: Katherine's workout program + Advertising other companies products + either Live events or Multi-influencer (candidate must justify choice). The three selected must sum to ≤20 hrs/week and ≥$30M profit.

math.setup: For each option: App Revenue = Customers(000s) × 1000 × Annual Rev/Customer. SM Impact = % × $5,000,000. Profit = App Revenue + SM Impact − Annual Cost. Profit/hr uses Katherine's hrs/week as denominator (annual profit basis).
steps: Katherine's workout program: Rev = 400,000 × $30 = $12M; SM impact = +10% × $5M = +$0.5M; Profit = $12M + $0.5M − $1M = $11.5M; Profit/hr = $11.5M / 5 = $2.3M/hr (2nd best)
Advertising other companies product: Rev = 250,000 × $25 = $6.25M; SM impact = 0; Profit = $6.25M − $0.25M = $6M; Profit/hr = $6M / 0.5 = $12M/hr (best)
Live events and in-app ticket portal: Rev = 250,000 × $90 = $22.5M; SM impact = +10% × $5M = +$0.5M; Profit = $22.5M + $0.5M − $7M = $16M; Profit/hr = $16M / 10 = $1.6M/hr (3rd best)
Multi-influencer workout program: Rev = 700,000 × $30 = $21M; SM impact = 0; Profit = $21M − $3M = $18M; Profit/hr = $18M / 12 = $1.5M/hr (4th best)
Creating and advertising private label products: Rev = 250,000 × $60 = $15M; SM impact = −30% × $5M = −$1.5M; Profit = $15M − $1.5M − $5.5M = $8M; Profit/hr = $8M / 8 = $1M/hr (worst)
Combination check — top 3 by profit/hr (Advertising + Workout + Live events): total profit = $6M + $11.5M + $16M = $33.5M ≥ $30M; total hrs = 0.5 + 5 + 10 = 15.5 hrs/week ≤ 20 hrs. MEETS BOTH GOALS.

Alternative: replace Live events with Multi-influencer: profit = $6M + $11.5M + $18M = $35.5M ≥ $30M; hrs = 0.5 + 5 + 12 = 17.5 hrs/week ≤ 20 hrs. ALSO MEETS BOTH GOALS. Candidate must argue for one over the other — Live events is more time-efficient (lower hours) while Multi-influencer yields higher total profit.
math.answer: Katherine should include Advertising other companies products ($12M/hr), Katherine's workout program ($2.3M/hr), and either Live events or Multi-influencer. Either combo clears the $30M profit and 20 hr/week thresholds.

brainstorming.prompt: What sorts of products and services could Katherine include on the app?

categories.name: Content / Workouts
ideas: Structured workout regimen with daily lessons

categories.name: Commerce / Products
ideas: Affiliate links to third-party fitness products

categories.name: Events / Community
ideas: In-person event announcements and ticket sales
Community forum or social feed within the app

categories.name: Platform / Network
ideas: Multi-influencer platform hosting other fitness creators

categories.name: Personalization / Lifestyle
ideas: Personal lifestyle content (travel, pets, daily routine)
Customized workout plans based on user goals
Premium subscription tier for exclusive access

recommendation: Katherine should launch the app, including her own workout program, advertising other companies' products, and either live events or multi-influencer workouts (candidate selects and justifies one). This combination generates approximately $33.5M–$35.5M in additional annual profit while requiring 15.5–17.5 hours per week of her time — meeting both goals.
risks: Difficulty launching and maintaining an app (technical and operational complexity)
Live events is heavily operationally intensive and may not be as polished as her pre-crafted social media content
Having multiple influencers on the app could dilute Katherine's brand or create partner management challenges
Optimal product/service selection is highly dependent on revenue, cost, and time estimates, which are preliminary
next_steps: Partner with an app development and maintenance team to build and sustain the platform
Identify companies and products to advertise and cultivate her workouts into an app-based regimen
Depending on selection: map out a live-event program OR identify and onboard other influencers to bring onto the platform
